html:
The largest trade fair in the Russian Empire, held each summer at Nizhny Novgorod, where the Oka river meets the Volga.

It began at the Makaryev monastery down the river, but after fire destroyed the old site in 1816 it moved to Nizhny Novgorod in 1817. The state built a large market town on the river bank, with rows of shops, warehouses and a cathedral.

River boats and later railways brought goods from all over Eurasia. Tea from China came by way of Kyakhta, cotton and silk from Central Asia and Persia, furs from Siberia, metal from the Urals, and cloth and machines from Moscow and Europe. Prices set at the fair shaped Russian trade for the year, and it was said that Nizhny Novgorod was Russia's pocket.

In 1896 it hosted the great All Russian Exhibition. The Soviet government closed the fair in 1930, as private trade ended. It was revived as an exhibition centre after the end of the Soviet Union.
sum: The largest trade fair in the Russian Empire, held each summer at Nizhny Novgorod, where the Oka river meets the Volga.
